title: Quantum Biology
description: Photosynthesis, enzymes and migrating birds all use quantum coherence. Unlocks quantum chlorophyll and magnetoreceptors.

puzzle.goal: An electron of energy E inside a protein meets a region of width L where the potential energy V is higher than E. Inside, its wavefunction decays instead of oscillating, with a local decay rate √(2m(V−E))/ħ. Write the probability of getting through, accumulating that decay across the barrier.
puzzle.name: WKB tunnelling probability
puzzle.form: exp ( - 2 / ħ * int ( 0 , L , sqrt ( 2 * m * ( V - E ) ) , x ) )
puzzle.ask: For a flat barrier the integral is just κħL with κ = √(2m(V−E))/ħ. Find the tunnelling probability through a 0.3 nm protein barrier with κ = 10 nm⁻¹.
puzzle.method: Assume the wavefunction is e^(±∫κ(x)dx) with slowly varying κ; the probability is the squared amplitude ratio, so the exponent doubles.
